title: Author deletes a memory while the partner is reading it
preconditions: A authored a memory that B has opened.
A deletes it from their own device.
B refreshes or navigates back to the memory.
expected_behavior: Only the author can delete the memory.
B no longer sees it after refresh; an already-open detail reports that it is unavailable.
The deletion does not affect B's ability to read other shared memories.
candidate_failure_modes: B can still edit or delete A's memory.
The open detail shows stale content indefinitely or crashes.
Deleting the memory deletes unrelated media still used elsewhere.

observed_code_behavior: Memory create is idempotent per (space_id, client_id) while the row is live.
Update and delete compare the observed updatedAt; a stale write returns 409 without side effects.
Authorship and authorName are computed per viewer, not stored as a snapshot.
documented_requirement: Only the author can delete the memory.
B no longer sees it after refresh; an already-open detail reports that it is unavailable.
The deletion does not affect B's ability to read other shared memories.
hypothetical_user_behavior:
A fictional participant (Jules Park) said: "Ran this audit on the offline/account paths I actually use. Answers to "why does this even exist?", in order of how fast I wanted it gone:

1. The persistent account indicator. It sits on every screen and tells me the thing Settings already tells me on demand. Break if removed: nothing — the account is one tap away, and the label is a static string, not state. Cost: it looks like a status, so I keep reading it as one and looking for meaning that isn't there.

2. The "Saving…" toast, layered on top of a pending-save badge, layered on top of a spinner. Three controls for one fact. Break if removed: nothing; the badge already carries count and retry affordance. Cost: the toast steals the bottom of the screen and moves nothing forward. Also it ignores reduced motion — it slides in regardless of the setting, which is exactly the decorative motion that hides state.

3. The "Last synced 3 min ago" line. It recomputes on foregrounding, not on a successful sync, so it's confidently wrong. Break if removed: nothing but a lie. Cost: false confidence in a path where confidence is the whole point.

What I'd keep: the pending-save count. One integer, one source of truth, same label everywhere. If I had to defend a single line of that whole path, it's that one.

Removed, not redesigned. Nothing above needs a replacement — it needs deletion."
Jules Park assumes: the sky is not the archive
Jules Park assumes: a setting applies immediately
Mina Sol assumes: a heading is a heading
Mina Sol assumes: a button that looks disabled is disabled
